A1.justification: Both complete, readable 20-page PDFs describe OS-Sentinel, MobileRisk-Live, and MobileRisk. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–D support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original safety-detection experiments in Tables 1–2, component and category analyses in Figures 5–7, and dataset analyses and case studies in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments, component and category analyses, and appendix analyses and case studies.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same hash, keyword, and pattern checks, contextual judge, step-level and trajectory-level procedures, and OR-based hybrid verdict. The expanded preliminary explanation introduces no method component or procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same MobileRisk and MobileRisk-Live tasks, applications, and ten risk categories. The benchmark construction and appendix coverage tables are unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same Rule-based Evaluators and LLM/VLM-as-a-Judge comparisons under corresponding backbones. Comparator membership in the component and category analyses also remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The scoring procedures, model configurations, benchmark construction, and 104-instruction live/frozen comparison are retained. Section 6 newly identifies its unsafe-only analysis subset without reporting a revision to the underlying experiment.

E4.justification: The component comparisons, category analysis, instruction-diversity visualization, trajectory statistics, and Appendix D case studies are retained. The added explanation of the analysis subset supplies no new analytical evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-run uncertainty estimates. Figure 8 retains the same statement that t-SNE seeds are randomly sampled for each plot.

E6.justification: All tabulated values and plotted data are unchanged, but v2 Section 6.1 adds a finding of '>80% accuracy' on unsafe cases. The corresponding Figure 5 still shows approximately 73–75% for OS-Sentinel, creating an inconsistent textual result claim.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 clarifies observation notation and explicitly states the any-unsafe-step criterion already present in v1's trajectory description and Appendix Prompt 12. The scoring and hybrid aggregation mathematics are retained; no substantive assumption, theorem, or proof changes.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same infrastructure and hybrid-detection contributions and performance claims. The introductory safety definition clarifies the existing scope without redefining these core contributions.

C2.justification: v2 frames Section 6 as targeting unsafe trajectories and removes v1's attribution of F1 differences to false positives, retaining differences in observation processing as the explanation. Section 3.1 also clarifies system-level versus contextual risks. The limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly discloses that the Section 6 analyses use unsafe instances. Implementation descriptions, annotation instructions, evaluation prompts, and code/data access information remain unchanged. This disclosure does not establish that the experiments changed.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, and complete reference list are unchanged after matching text across page breaks. Research positioning and novelty claims are retained.

P1.justification: v2 locally rewrites the introduction and Section 3.1, adds analysis framing, and removes the duplicated live/frozen comparison paragraph. It also deletes the data-compliance statement and AI-assistance disclosure. The overall organization and appendix content remain stable.

P2.justification: Figures and tables retain their content and visual encodings, but placement changes: Figure 4 moves from page 5 to page 6, and Figure 7 from page 8 to page 9. Other figures and surrounding text undergo limited reflow.

improvement.justification: The clearer safety definition, analysis-subset disclosure, and removal of duplicated prose help readers. However, v2 introduces an unsupported '>80% accuracy' statement in Section 6.1 that conflicts with the unchanged Figure 5 values of approximately 73–75%. This concrete reporting inconsistency outweighs the limited clarity gains.
